## Resolving a vector into components {#iv2-resolving .component-lesson .vector-lesson}

The angle <span data-math="\theta"></span> is measured anticlockwise from the positive <span data-math="x"></span>-axis.

<div data-components="resolving"></div>
<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet Section 3.2.1 · p. 18</div>

::: notes
Use a positive first-quadrant angle to connect the horizontal component with adjacent/hypotenuse=cos θ and vertical with sin θ. Then cross 90 degrees and predict the sign change. The radius stays 6, so a=6cosθ i+6sinθ j. The old component slides had sine and cosine swapped; this diagram and formula correct that. At 150 degrees, x=−3√3≈−5.20 and y=3. The adjacent signed component is negative; a triangle side length itself is non-negative.
:::
